That feature is called **Inline Completion** (commonly referred to as **"Ghost Text"** or **"AI Code Suggestions"**).

Unlike a traditional dropdown menu (which completes individual variable or function names from your LSP), inline completion predicts and suggests entire statements, lines, or blocks of code ahead of your cursor in faint, gray text that you can accept by pressing `<Tab>`.

---

### Key Forms of This Feature

1. **AI Inline Completion (Full Sentences & Logic)**  
   Uses an LLM to predict the rest of your statement, line, or multi-line block based on your surrounding code and comments.
   - **[GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/zbirenbaum/copilot.lua)** (`copilot.lua`): The industry standard; requires a GitHub Copilot subscription.
   - **[Supermaven](https://github.com/supermaven-inc/supermaven-nvim)** (`supermaven-nvim`): Extremely fast with low latency and a capable free tier.
   - **[Codeium](https://github.com/Exafunction/codeium.nvim)** (`codeium.nvim`): A popular, free-for-individuals alternative to GitHub Copilot.

2. **LSP Ghost Text (Completion Preview)**  
   Since your Neovim setup already uses **`blink.cmp`**, you can also enable its built-in `ghost_text = { enabled = true }` option. This previews the currently selected suggestion directly in the buffer as ghost text before you confirm it.
